title: bug: JetBrains protected selection with a UNC project base (\\localhost\C$\…\project) treats local project paths as outside it
description: Inverse of task-526a2080 (which refuses UNC/device CANDIDATES only). When basePath itself is UNC (\\localhost\C$\…\project, \\127.0.0.1\C$\…, \\wsl$\…), RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject/select build project forms via toRealPath, which keeps UNC, so a local C:\…\project PATH entry or a node physically inside the project reads as outside. VS Code twin reproduced by qa-ba3f4f35 on RF06b (UNC_PROJECT_LEAKS=2; mem:gotcha-protected-windows-unc-project-base). Raised in comments on task-526a2080 by governor-693b7073 and architect-6fc3dd5c; not in 526a2080's approved plan. Fix direction: under protected on Windows, refuse when either project form is not isPlainLocalPath (parity with VS Code's "refuse, never canonicalize"); decide \\wsl$ projects explicitly. May fold into task-1c2bfeca if file identity covers it.
definitionOfDone: On a Windows host, isOutsideProject(localProjectPath, uncSpellingOfProject) is false and select refuses a node/installed artifact inside the project when the base is a UNC spelling; shown by JetBrains unit tests needing no network for the refusal path.

implementationPlan.description:
Production change, one file: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt. The rule: under the protected switch on a Windows host, nothing is provably outside a project base that is not a plain local base.

First re-read the file as its two dependencies landed it:
- task-526a2080 reopen 1 added the `profile: RuntimeProfile` parameter on the internal overloads of installedArtifact, installedExecutable, isOutsideProject and select. That is the switch: LEGACY, including Restart Daemon's stop selection through MoeDaemonSupervisor.stopCommandOrNull, skips every plain-local check.
- task-1c2bfeca at 1f19140c added outsideByIdentity, `val real by lazy { resolve(path) }` and the identity branch in select.
If 1c2bfeca is reopened and lands differently, keep the invariants, not the line numbers.

(a) Constants:
- `BASE_NOT_PLAIN = "the project directory is not a plain local Windows path"`, verbatim. VS Code RF06b uses the same string, so TROUBLESHOOTING needs one entry.
- `LOCAL_DRIVE_TYPES`: WinBase.DRIVE_REMOVABLE, DRIVE_FIXED, DRIVE_CDROM and DRIVE_RAMDISK.

(b) One allow-list. isPlainLocalPath(path, windows) also requires that no segment of comparablePath(path, false), split on '/', ends in '.' or ' '.
- Do not exempt '.' or '..': a spelling that still holds them fails closed.
- Candidates get the rule through the existing calls: the normalized spelling and the real path in isOutsideProject, and the real path in select.
- N5's rows keep their answers. `\\.\C:\proj` stays plain because comparablePath strips the prefix first.
- KDoc: Win32 drops a trailing '.' or ' ' from a segment when it reads a path, so `<tmp>\project.` names `<tmp>\project`. toRealPath returns such a name as written at a reparse point. In the probe, a junction to a literal `project.` folder resolved to `<tmp>\project.`, and re-opening that string read `<tmp>\project`.

(c) Drive type:
- Add `@Volatile internal var driveType: (String) -> Int`. Its default is a private val `{ Kernel32.INSTANCE.GetDriveType(it) }` (JNA, com.sun.jna.platform.win32, in the platform's util-8.jar; the platform's own WindowsRoots uses it). resetForTest restores the default.
- Add a private `isPlainLocalBase(path: String): Boolean`. It holds when isPlainLocalPath(path) holds and, on a Windows host only, driveType of the path's drive root (`X:\`, taken from comparablePath(path, false)) is in LOCAL_DRIVE_TYPES. An Exception or a LinkageError (JNA not loadable) answers false.
- Only a drive root `X:\` is ever passed. GetDriveType answers a drive letter from the logon session's device map without opening the volume: in the probe, a letter defined to the unreachable `\\192.0.2.1\nosuch` answered DRIVE_REMOTE in 0 ms. A UNC root is opened (`\\192.0.2.1\nosuch\` blocked for more than 20 s), but the spelling check has already refused every UNC form.
- KDoc: toRealPath keeps a mapped drive letter (`U:\…` stays `U:\…`), and FileStore.type() reads the remote NTFS, so only the drive type shows a network drive. A subst letter reports its target's type and stays plain; 1c2bfeca's identity judges it.

(d) isOutsideProject (internal overload). New order; every new check runs only when profile == PROTECTED:
1. Paths.get(path), a pure parse, then candidate.isAbsolute and the candidate's plain spelling. These are unchanged.
2. NEW: isPlainLocalBase(basePath) on the raw base spelling. It is the first thing that touches the base: no Paths.get(basePath), toRealPath, isSameFile or other lookup comes before it. JDK 17's Paths.get throws InvalidPathException on a trailing space, while JBR 25's does not.
3. Only then `project = realPathOrNull(basePath)` and the `projects` forms. Today they are built first, so move them after.
4. NEW: when project != null, isPlainLocalBase(project.toString()). A real base that is not plain answers false, for example a junction to `project.` or a link to a share.
5. The existing forms check, `real` and 1c2bfeca's identity conjunct stay unchanged. Identity now runs only for a plain local base.
- Under LEGACY none of the new checks runs. On POSIX they are no-ops.
- Keep both catches (Exception and IOError answer false). A block body with early returns is fine.
- KDoc: on a Windows host under protected, the base must also be a plain local base, both as written (checked before any lookup) and as its real path. Otherwise nothing is provably outside it.

(e) select:
- Before realPathOrNull(basePath): `if (profile == RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED && !isPlainLocalBase(basePath)) return rejected(BASE_NOT_PLAIN, basePath)`.
- Right after the project resolves: the same check on project.toString(), returning `rejected(BASE_NOT_PLAIN, project)`.
- Both come before resolve(), so no candidate is resolved for a refused base. A plain base that cannot be resolved keeps 'the project directory cannot be resolved'.
- Add one comment with the why. toRealPath keeps a share or device base and a mapped letter, and nothing maps them back to a local folder. File identity can match a loopback share, but only by opening it, and a foreign redirector (\\wsl$ 9P, third-party SMB) need not report NTFS file ids. So the refusal comes from the spelling and the drive type, like VS Code's 'refuse, never canonicalize'.
- This covers node (installedExecutable) and daemon, wrapper and proxy (installedArtifact), and through them protectedDaemonCommand, TerminalAgentLauncher and ManagedVmPanel.

(f) In usableStore's debug line, change 'the IDE state store is inside the project' to 'the IDE state store is not provably outside the project'.

Do not change MoeDaemonSupervisor, ProtectedStateStore, TerminalAgentLauncher, ManagedVmPanel, projectKey, profile() or outsideByIdentity. There is no \\wsl$ carve-out, and no new parameter on any selector.

Build, one file: moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts. The unit-test JVM must load JNA. Otherwise step 1's default drive lookup fails closed, and every protected Windows row that reaches a base check breaks: S1, S8, S9, N8, MoeDaemonSupervisorTest's W33, and the PS/PP rows that go through usableFor, among others.

Why it does not load today:
- tasks.test's doFirst (lines 124-133) removes IntelliJPlatformArgumentProvider. That provider would pass product-info.json's launch arguments, including `-Djna.boot.library.path=%IDE_HOME%/lib/jna/amd64`.
- util-8.jar carries JNA's classes but no jnidispatch.
- Probe on JDK 17.0.20 with util-8.jar on the classpath: without the property, Kernel32 throws UnsatisfiedLinkError, then NoClassDefFoundError. With it, GetDriveType(C:\) = 3.

Change:
- In `tasks { test { … } }`, outside doFirst, add exactly one system property: `jna.boot.library.path` = intellijPlatform.platformPath.resolve("lib/jna/" + System.getProperty("os.arch")).toString(). The Windows x64 IDE ships `lib/jna/amd64/jnidispatch.dll`.
- Keep the existing jvmArgs and the doFirst block. Do not re-add IntelliJPlatformArgumentProvider or any other launch argument.
- The value must come from intellijPlatform.platformPath, never from a hard-coded cache path.
- Add one comment: the IDE launcher passes this path, and the provider removed below would have passed it too. RuntimeSelectionPolicy's drive lookup and its test junctions need it.
- Step 4's default-lookup assertion and every existing protected Windows row prove it took effect.

comments.author: governor-693b7073
comments.content:
@architect-6fc3dd5c Planning input from architect-4ae016fb (526a2080's planner, msg-98faf485, 16:40Z, by code reading, unprobed). It is not a DoD edit; this row's 2-item DoD stands, and the planner decides scope.
Confirmed gap at acdcd627: isOutsideProject (RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt:271) builds both base forms (normalize + toRealPath) and never runs isPlainLocalPath on them. select (:285) takes project = toRealPath(basePath) unchecked. Both lines predate acdcd627.
Proposed scope, parity with RF06b's "refuse, never canonicalize":
(1) Under protected on a Windows host, select, installedArtifact and installedExecutable refuse with a named reason, before resolving any candidate, when either base form fails isPlainLocalPath. No spawn.
(2) isOutsideProject returns false whenever either base form is not plainly local.
(3) \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost bases are refused too, with no carve-out, since \\wsl$\<distro>\mnt\<drive>\… aliases a local drive. TROUBLESHOOTING.md says what a WSL-hosted project does instead.
(4) Tests need no network. Legacy, POSIX and local-base rows are unchanged.
Extra fact, a possible silent downgrade: projectKey (:169) keys RF02's profile record off the real path. Open a project that has a stored PROTECTED record through a UNC spelling, and the record reads ABSENT. If project.json no longer declares verified-local, profile() returns LEGACY with no downgrade prompt, so rule (1) never runs. It needs a human to open through a share. Decide whether this row covers it or files it.
Ordering: this row dependsOn 526a2080 (in QA) and 1c2bfeca (planned around file identity, same file). Check what 1c2bfeca's outsideByIdentity already covers before you add code.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Under the protected profile on a Windows host, a project base that is not a plain local base has nothing provably outside it. One allow-list, isPlainLocalPath, now serves candidates and bases alike: a form is plainly local when it is drive-qualified (X:\, optionally behind \\?\ or \\.\) and no segment ends in '.' or ' '. That rejects '.', '..', a trailing dot and a trailing space, which Win32 would drop on read. A base form must also lie on a local drive: GetDriveType of its drive root must be removable, fixed, CD-ROM or RAM disk. Remote, unknown, no-root or a failing lookup all refuse. Both the raw base spelling, checked before any lookup, and the base's real path must pass. For a base that does not:
- isOutsideProject answers false for every path, so the protected PATH keeps nothing and ProtectedStateStore.usableFor is false;
- select refuses node, daemon, wrapper and proxy with exactly 'the project directory is not a plain local Windows path', so nothing spawns.
This covers UNC shares (\\localhost\C$\…, \\127.0.0.1\C$\…, //host/share/…), device paths, \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost, rooted and drive-relative spellings, dot and space spellings, a junction whose real path ends in '.', and a mapped network drive letter, whose letter toRealPath keeps. Under protected, a candidate whose normalized spelling or real path has such a segment is now refused too. With the switch off (LEGACY, including Restart Daemon's stop selection), on POSIX and for plain local bases on local drives, every answer is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: On Windows, isOutsideProject(p, base) is false for every nonLocalBases spelling. p ranges over the project, a folder inside it, a missing folder inside it and an unrelated outside folder. Neither a throwing candidate resolver nor a throwing drive lookup is reached, the defaults give the same answer, and store.usableFor(base) is false.

On Windows, installedExecutable and installedArtifact refuse an in-project and an outside node or root with exactly 'the project directory is not a plain local Windows path' for every non-plain base. protectedDaemonEnvironment empties PATH. A supervisor through the volume-GUID base spawns nothing and shows the message, and PROTECTED stopCommandOrNull is null.

A junction to a literal <tmp>\project. folder: as the base, it is refused with that reason and isOutsideProject is false; as a candidate path, the node behind it is refused with 'node executable is not a plain local Windows path'.

With the drive lookup answering DRIVE_REMOTE, DRIVE_UNKNOWN or DRIVE_NO_ROOT_DIR, or throwing an Exception or a LinkageError, a plain local base is refused with that reason and nothing spawns. Removable, fixed, CD-ROM and RAM disk accept. The lookup only ever receives the base's drive root, and in the unit-test JVM the default lookup answers a local type for the temp drive.
LEGACY: stopCommandOrNull for a volume-GUID base and for a plain base returns the installed stop command, and no drive lookup happens.
isPlainLocalPath(windows = true) is false for any segment ending in '.' or ' ', including '.', '..' and a \\?\-prefixed form. It is true for inner dots and spaces, and POSIX is unchanged.
Existing rows pass unchanged, including task-526a2080's and task-1c2bfeca's, and the JetBrains gradle test run exits 0.
invariants: No filesystem call or drive lookup touches the base before the raw spelling check, in isOutsideProject or select. driveType never receives a UNC root.
The base checks (spelling, real path, drive type) run if and only if profile == PROTECTED, the same switch as the candidate plain-local checks, and they act only on a Windows host.
isOutsideProject never throws, and select never throws. A drive lookup that throws an Exception or a LinkageError refuses.
On POSIX isPlainLocalPath is always true and no drive lookup runs.
Refusal reasons never contain a path; only the log gets it.
compatibility: isOutsideProject, installedArtifact and installedExecutable keep the signatures task-526a2080 landed (protected-default public wrappers and internal RuntimeProfile overloads), with no new parameter. The drive lookup is an internal @Volatile var like store and confirmer, and resetForTest restores it.
A plain base that cannot be resolved keeps 'the project directory cannot be resolved'.
Restart Daemon's LEGACY stop selection (MoeDaemonSupervisor.stopCommandOrNull, protectedNode, stopBuilder) behaves exactly as before.
The unit-test JVM gains only -Djna.boot.library.path, the IDE launcher's value. IntelliJPlatformArgumentProvider stays removed.
approvedScope: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isPlainLocalPath: no segment may end in '.' or ' '
RuntimeSelectionPolicy: BASE_NOT_PLAIN, LOCAL_DRIVE_TYPES, an internal @Volatile driveType whose default is JNA Kernel32.GetDriveType, a private isPlainLocalBase, and resetForTest restoring driveType
RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject (internal overload): the raw base check before any lookup, and the real base check after realPathOrNull(basePath)
RuntimeSelectionPolicy.select: the raw base check before realPathOrNull(basePath) and the real base check after it, both with BASE_NOT_PLAIN
build.gradle.kts tasks.test: one system property, jna.boot.library.path
RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest: helpers nonLocalBases, rawJunction and withDottedJunction; rows N9, N10, S10, S11 and S12
reuse: isPlainLocalPath, comparablePath, isWithin, realPathOrNull and rejected(), the RuntimeProfile switch from task-526a2080's reopen, and outsideByIdentity from task-1c2bfeca, unchanged

JNA from the platform's util-8.jar: Kernel32.GetDriveType and WinBase.DRIVE_*, as the platform's own com.intellij.execution.wsl.WindowsRoots uses them. The test junction uses Kernel32.CreateFile/DeviceIoControl, WinioctlUtil.FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT and WinNT.IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT
Test helpers share(), volumeSpelling(), protectedFixture(), installedLayout(), supervisorFor(), assertRejected(), realFile() and exitOf()
sourceAssumptions: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt at 1f19140c (task-1c2bfeca): isPlainLocalPath (202-203) checks only the drive. The internal isOutsideProject (284-308) builds project and projects before the candidate checks. select (311-336) resolves the project first. usableStore is at 509-514 and resetForTest at 610-614.

build.gradle.kts tasks.test (121-134) removes IntelliJPlatformArgumentProvider in doFirst, so the JDK 17 test JVM gets none of the IDE's -Djna.* launch args. util-8.jar holds JNA classes but no jnidispatch; lib/jna/amd64 holds it.

Probe 2026-10-30, D:\arch-52fb-r3-probe, JDK 17.0.20 + util-8.jar. Without jna.boot.library.path, Kernel32 throws UnsatisfiedLinkError. With it, GetDriveType gives C:\ 3, D:\ 3, subst 3, a net use of \\localhost\D$ 4, an unused letter 1, and a letter DefineDosDevice'd to \\192.0.2.1\nosuch 4 in 0 ms. The UNC root \\192.0.2.1\nosuch\ blocked over 20 s.

Same probe: mklink /J and PowerShell New-Item -ItemType Junction drop a trailing '.' from the target. A FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT mount point with substitute name \??\<tmp>\project. keeps it, and toRealPath(link) = <tmp>\project.. Re-opening that string reads <tmp>\project (isSameFile is true).

toRealPath keeps a mapped drive letter (U:\…), isSameFile(mapped, local) is true for a loopback share, and FileStore.type() reads NTFS. JDK 17's Paths.get throws InvalidPathException on a trailing space; JBR 25's does not.
MoeDaemonSupervisorTest's alias rows (W31-W35) alias only candidates. Every base there and in the existing policy rows is a plain local temp folder or, in N8 and S9, a subst letter (DRIVE_FIXED).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rev 3 keeps rev 2's base refusal and folds in the governor's points 3 and 4 (comment-41cd2cfa).
(1) Chosen: the drive type through JNA. Kernel32.GetDriveType is the platform's own route (WindowsRoots). A drive root is answered from the device map without I/O; this was probed, including an unreachable target. That settles the governor's blocking risk, so no divergence fallback is needed.
(2) Rejected: reflection into sun.nio.fs.WindowsNativeDispatcher. Both JVMs open sun.nio.fs, so it would need no build change, but it puts JDK internals into security code.
(3) Rejected: public NIO. FileStore exposes only volume:isRemovable and volume:isCdrom, and type() reads the remote NTFS.
(4) Rejected: a test-only fake as the default lookup, to avoid the build change. Other test classes reach protected selection without injecting one, and the JNA path would go untested.
(5) Rejected by probe: a mklink /J or PowerShell junction for the '.' row. Both drop the trailing dot; a raw FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT mount point keeps it.
(6) Rejected: 8.3 short names as the 'plain spelling, dot real path' stand-in. They depend on the host.
(7) Out of scope: the drive check on candidates. The governor's point 4 is base-only; this is recorded as a residual divergence from VS Code.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- tasks.test strips IntelliJPlatformArgumentProvider, so the unit-test JVM (JDK 17 toolchain) lacks every IDE launch arg. That includes jna.boot.library.path; JNA's natives live in <IDE>/lib/jna/<arch>, not in util-8.jar.
- The test JVM is JDK 17, where Paths.get throws on a trailing space. The IDE runs JBR 25, which accepts it. The raw base check must precede any Paths.get(basePath).
- Java's toRealPath calls GetFinalPathNameByHandle only at a reparse point. It keeps subst and mapped letters, returns a junction target as written (`project.` kept), and otherwise applies GetFullPathName, which drops a trailing dot.
- Kernel32 in util-8 has CreateDirectory and DeleteFile but no RemoveDirectory, so the test cleans up a dot folder with cmd rd and a \\?\ path. Java's Paths.get rejects '?'.
- ensureMoeInitialized touches <base>\.moe, so supervisor rows use the volume-GUID base (local), not a share.
- java.io.File keeps the \\.\Volume{…} and UNC prefixes. IntelliJ's basePath uses forward slashes (//localhost/D$/…).
planningNotes.risks:
- 1c2bfeca is still in flux. Re-read the landed code first, and keep the semantic invariant (the base checks run iff the candidate checks run, under PROTECTED), not the line numbers.
- If the build property does not take effect, every protected Windows row that expects acceptance fails closed. S12's default-lookup assertion names the cause.
- JUnit's TemporaryFolder cannot delete a dot-ending folder, so withDottedJunction must clean up in finally through \\?\.
- S11's hazard assertion relies on short temp paths. Java adds \\?\ past about 248 characters, which disables Win32 normalization.
- volumeSpelling needs mountvol. S10 skips without it, like S8; the verification host has it.
- RED runs may contact the local SMB server, or \\wsl$ for a missing distro. Both fail fast, and GREEN contacts neither.
- From WSL, run cmd.exe probes in single quotes, or bash collapses \\.
- Accepted cost: protected Windows projects opened through any alias, or on a mapped drive, start nothing, and their state is session-only.
